dependency_notes: S1 is foundational and load-bearing: nothing in the app compiles or runs against 0.7.0 types until both fork SHAs are installed (spec §2 blackout). S2 and S3 both depend on S1 for that reason. S2 and S3 are otherwise functionally independent (KeyPackage slot lifecycle vs dispatcher/epochResolver wiring) but both touch app/src/context/MarmotContext.tsx at disjoint line ranges (:1219/:1390/:1410 slot sites for S2, :1699/:1824 dispatcher wiring for S3) — landing S2 before S3 (story_order, not a hard schema dependency) avoids the two stories editing the same file in the same window. S4 is the FR-A7 cross-cutting integration story: architecture.md's own 'Risk concentration' note places all four AC-ORDER-* guarantees on files S3 already owns (applicationRumorDispatcher.ts, epochResolver.ts) plus the unchanged-but-interacting welcomeSubscription.ts, so S4's dependency union reduces to {S3} — it is still emitted as its own story per FR-A7 because the signal (architecture.md §6 + acceptance-criteria.md's 'Spans modules:' lines) is present, not because the guarantees are architecturally scattered. S5 (behavior docs) depends on S3 because it documents the 'authenticity: mls' behavior S3 lands; it has no dependency on S4 and could be sequenced anywhere after S3, but is placed last for readability.
mock_resolution_plan: No temporary mocks are introduced by this epic. All story dependencies are real, sequential landings (S1's fork pin must exist before S2/S3 can compile; S3's dispatcher wiring must exist before S4 can exercise real producers) rather than mocked seams — consistent with Module Ownership principle 1's exception for a story that is naturally sequenced instead of independently testable in isolation, and with the FR-A7 integration story's Mock Strategy exception (S4 verifies against S3's real, already-implemented producers and must never mock them).

stories.name: pin-marmot-ts-fork-dependencies
stories.title: Pin ts-mls and marmot-ts to the authenticated-sender fork SHAs
stories.description: Pin app/package.json's ts-mls and @internet-privacy/marmot-ts dependencies to the two load-bearing fork commit SHAs already resolved in spec.md §5 (github:941design/ts-mls#9f0c7bd251429f6e56bc7a41c86d7d3e74b27b13, github:941design/marmot-ts#cb0025c0ae3ffd053bf4a6ec528869716148ffb2), and prove — not merely assert — that a cold `make node_modules` resolves both over HTTPS (never git+ssh) and that exactly one ts-mls copy, the fork's, is what actually installed. This is the foundational story: per spec.md §2, without the fork's senderCredential every group application message is silently dropped (total blackout), invisible to typecheck — nothing downstream compiles or behaves correctly until this lands. The story pins and proves the two SHAs; it does not decide them (already decided, spec §5).

stories.name: order-sensitive-ingest-integration-verification
stories.title: Verify order-sensitive ingest-and-authenticate guarantees across dispatcher, epochResolver, and welcomeSubscription
stories.description: FR-A7 integration story. Proves, via property/interleaving tests against S3's real, already-landed dispatcher and epochResolver, the four whole-flow guarantees architecture.md §6 names for the inbound-application-rumor-ingest-and-authenticate flow: sender-mismatched rumors never reach markSeen in either dedup layer; a rejected:unauthenticated-sender outcome is never treated as bufferable/retriable; EpochResolver's onApplicationMessage callback stays a no-op through competing-commit rollback/replay; and historical-sync/live-subscription overlap never produces divergent authenticity outcomes for the same rumor id. Runs last relative to its dependency (S3) because it verifies the assembled whole against real producers, not mocks.

includes: Property/interleaving test generating orderings of {legitimate rumor, sender-mismatched rumor sharing an id, redelivery of that id} across the dispatcher's per-group LRU and welcomeSubscription's raw-event-id dedup sets, asserting the mismatched rumor is never recorded in either structure and the legitimate rumor is processed exactly once regardless of arrival order (AC-ORDER-1)

Property test generating ingest() outcome sequences containing at least one rejected:'unauthenticated-sender' at an arbitrary position among unreadable/skipped/processed results, asserting it is never added to EpochResolver's retry buffer and never triggers welcomeSubscription's un-mark-on-buffered logic (AC-ORDER-2)

Test asserting that for any ordering of competing-commit rollback and replay within the 3s grace window, every re-emitted application message routes authenticity resolution exclusively through authenticatedApplicationMessage, with EpochResolver's onApplicationMessage callback remaining a zero-side-effect no-op in production configuration for every replayed message, independent of replay order/count (AC-ORDER-3)

Test asserting that for any interleaving where the same rumor id is observed by both welcomeSubscription's historical-sync path and the dispatcher's live subscription, both paths agree on the authenticity outcome (both 'mls' or both the same rejection reason) and deliver to handlers at most once (AC-ORDER-4)
excludes: Any new production behavior — this story verifies guarantees the epic's other stories are expected to already satisfy; a genuine gap found here is a defect against S2/S3, not new scope
Mocking applicationRumorDispatcher, epochResolver, or welcomeSubscription — per FR-A7's Mock Strategy exception this story verifies against S3's real, already-implemented producers

stories.notes: is_integration_story=true forces lighter_path=false per the mutual-exclusion invariant, regardless of the file-extension/AC-completeness predicates (this story's own test-only .ts file target would in any case classify as files_code, independently yielding false). owning_module is intentionally omitted per FR-A7 step 5 — this story spans applicationRumorDispatcher, epochResolver, and welcomeSubscription by design rather than owning exactly one. Dependency: S3 (the union of AC-ORDER-1..4's spanned_by sets in the top-level cross_cutting_acs array, all [S3]), so story_order places S4 after S3.
